## What it computes

$-x$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$z = \mathrm{RN}(-x).$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Target (not proved)

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z = \mathrm{RN}(-x)$: the number of the format nearest to $-x$, ties to even.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked.

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition neg_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x : R,
  fmt emin prec x ->
  let z := neg_1 x in
  fmt emin prec z /\
  z = RN emin prec (- x).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** a change of sign (milestone2.md, BallVector, bv_neg_k). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/neg_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/neg_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The negation of a number of T: exact. The step of bv_neg_1, the negation of a BallVector with
# one-limb centers (milestone2.md, "BallVector": bv_neg_k), whose two-limb step is neg_2.

z = neg(x)
```
